description: A music supervisor must make the binding music-clearance call for a festival's official trailer, selecting the usable recording and locking the cue, territory, credit, and delivery paperwork before the trailer is uploaded.

shared_context.S1: The festival's official trailer is picture-locked for a 60-second cut and is scheduled for upload this week.
shared_context.S2: The current music shortlist contains the tracks "Static Bloom" and "Neon Weather."
shared_context.S3: The trailer will be used in the festival's official online promotion and in festival-cinema pre-roll.
shared_context.S4: Mara makes the final music-clearance call and records the approved delivery package.
shared_context.S5: The production's standard clearance huddle gives rights, label, editorial, and festival-submissions leads a turn to report their findings before Mara records the decision.

PF1.text: Jonah reviewed the executed publishing license for "Static Bloom" and confirmed that the composition may be used in the official trailer only for a cue of no more than 42 seconds, with the exact credit "Written by Celia Voss"; he completed the review yesterday but has not yet entered the terms in the clearance tracker.

PF2.text: Leila confirmed with the master-rights owner that only the instrumental master of "Static Bloom" is cleared for this trailer, on a non-exclusive basis in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom; the vocal master and any other territory are excluded, and the confirmation is still in her email rather than the shared licensing folder.

PF3.text: Owen checked the locked picture and confirmed that the music cue begins at exactly 00:18 and runs for exactly 42 seconds; changing either timing would require reopening the approved picture lock, so he has not circulated a revised music note.

PF4.text: Rina confirmed with the festival upload vendor that the trailer package must include a 48 kHz, 24-bit stereo WAV of the cleared instrumental and a completed cue sheet before the file can be accepted; the vendor added this requirement to the submission portal this morning, but Rina has not updated the production checklist.

commitment_examples.detail: Submit the completed cue sheet with the approved trailer package.
Record the approved delivery package with the completed cue sheet included.

acceptance_conditions: The approved track must be "Static Bloom".
The approved recording must be the instrumental master.
The cue must begin at exactly 00:18.
The cue must run for exactly 42 seconds.
The license must cover exactly the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.
The credit must read exactly "Written by Celia Voss".
The delivery must identify a 48 kHz, 24-bit stereo WAV.
A cue sheet must be required and a commitment must mention its completion or submission.

content_checks.C2: (decisions['approved_version'] == 'instrumental master' or decisions['approved_version'] == 'Instrumental master' or decisions['approved_version'] == 'instrumental') and decisions['licensed_territories'] == ['United States', 'Canada', 'United Kingdom']
content_checks.C6: ('48 kHz' in decisions['audio_delivery']) and ('24-bit' in decisions['audio_delivery']) and ('stereo WAV' in decisions['audio_delivery'])
content_checks.C8: decisions['cue_sheet_required'] == True and any(('cue sheet' in c['detail'] or 'cue_sheet' in c['type']) and (('submission' in c['detail']) or ('submission' in c['type']) or ('completed' in c['detail']) or ('included' in c['detail']) or ('include' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The publishing license makes "Static Bloom" usable only with a cue no longer than exactly 42 seconds and the exact credit "Written by Celia Voss," rather than allowing an unrestricted shortlist choice.
The master-rights confirmation changes the recording to the instrumental master and fixes the licensed territory list to exactly the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.
The locked picture fixes the cue placement at exactly 00:18 for exactly 42 seconds, instead of leaving timing to a generic trailer edit.
The upload-vendor requirement changes delivery to a 48 kHz, 24-bit stereo WAV and requires both a cue sheet and a commitment documenting its completion or submission.
